_comment: ONLY add config to this file if it is INTEGRATION TEST related and you wish to override the config from the website
_layering_comment: This file is loaded, then appsettings.Integration.json on top of it. That second file is
gitignored, so anything it sets wins locally and is invisible in the repo - if a value here
seems to have no effect, look there first.
The DDS values below are the published sandbox credentials, so three of the four integration
tests run from a clean clone with no local file at all. The fourth,
ConsumerAccessTokenSettings - a real Entra client secret, which is NOT public and must stay in
_ConnectionStrings_comment: Its own database, deliberately. Every host and test suite used to point at the same LocalDB
'LondonFhirService', so running the suites concurrently - which is what 'dotnet test' on the
solution does - had them creating, seeding and deleting each other's rows, producing failures
that vanished on re-run in isolation. Each suite migrates its own database at startup via
Database.Migrate(), so no extra provisioning step is needed.
_LdsConfigurations_comment: LDS is registered in DI on every host, so its provider is constructed even when no test uses
it - and a placeholder baseUrl made that construction throw UriFormatException, which surfaced
as a 500 and failed every integration test. These values exist only to be well-formed.
The .invalid TLD is reserved by RFC 2606 and can never resolve, so nothing here can
accidentally reach a real endpoint. The integration tests activate only the DDS provider, so
LDS is never actually called. Populate real LDS values in appsettings.Integration.json when
there is an LDS environment to test against.
